text.p: China's Guangshen Railway Co Ltd has registered net profits of 1.178 billion yuan ($141.9 million) since it was transformed into a stockholding company in March last year, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The company outstripped other Chinese railway companies in average per kilometre operational railway earnings, per capita pre-tax earnings and per capita after-tax profits, it said.
The Guangshen Railway Co was transformed into a stockholding company in March 1996 to help it compete with domestic airlines which had lured passengers away from the country's railways, it said.
Since then, it had won back some of its lost market share and earned profits of 1.178 billion yuan after tax, it said without giving a figure for the whole of 1996.

The railway, which runs between the cities of Guangzhou and Shenzhen in China's southern Guangdong province, planned to introduce automatic ticket machines in the two cities to speed up sales, it said.

It would also complete the electrification of the existing Guangzhou-Shenzhen line and use imported trains made in Sweden to shorten the duration of a one-way journey to 48 minutes in the first half of next year, it said without giving further details.
Guangshen Railway was China's first state-owned stockholding company in the railway sector and the first Chinese firm ever to be listed on the New York and Hong Kong stock markets, it said.
In June this year, the company's chairman and chief accountant were dismissed after 300 million yuan was invested in a local finance company without the approval of the board of directors.
